newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Ethiopia vows to tighten coffee quality control.
newsitem.headline: Ethiopia vows to tighten coffee quality control.

text.p: Ethiopia will focus on tightening coffee quality control in the face of fierce international competition, a senior industry official said on Wednesday

Tsegaye Berhane, general manager of the Ethiopian Coffee and Tea Development Authority, told Reuters a recent visit to Latin America and Europe had clearly revealed that "Ethiopia must improve post harvest quality control in coffee."
Producers in Brazil, Guatemala and Costa Rica had shown an Ethiopian delegation the need for improved production, processing and marketing.
He said buyers of Ethiopian coffee stressed they wanted better quality and greater quantities of washed coffee, currently about 20 percent of total Ethiopian output.
Tsegaye said the authority would introduce an integrated package to help small-scale farmers increase yields and quality.
He said Ethiopia would promote research on disease-resistant coffee strains and encourage farmers to set up cooperatives.
Ethiopia concluded sales contracts for a total of 133,765 tonnes worth $409.4 million during the current fiscal year running from June 1996 to July 1997.
It had exported 117,979 tonnes worth $356.6 million last year.
The authority has forecast Ethiopia's coffee exports in 1997/98 at 128,040 tonnes, which would earn about $348 million.
